# refactor(config): split config I/O from policy and own retry defaults

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to the parent issue or its siblings.

## What

Settings files and the environment are still read the same way and give the same results, but the
code that decides what a setting means no longer reads files itself.

## Why

Configuration rules are mixed with file and directory access. That makes them hard to reuse from
anything other than the command line, and hard to test without a disk. Retry defaults also live with
business rules even though they are configurable values.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, GitHub, files, containers, terminal, logging), `app` (use cases) and `cli` (commands).
Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`,
the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and `docs/architecture.html`.

This issue implements one part of the design in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. That file is
in the repository; read the sections named below. Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow
the spec and say so in the PR.

## Don't undo these

- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image. The one exception:
  `jig init` saves a credential to `.jig/.env` (owner-only, git-ignored) after the operator agrees.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged unless this issue says otherwise.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Keep dependency policy in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with
  fixtures in `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.
- If you change where something lives, update `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md`
  and the code map in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and any guide that names a moved path. Describe current
  behavior in the present tense.

## Target

Spec sections: "Configuration and defaults", "Application preparation and resource lifetime".

- `src/config/load-config.ts` (`loadConfig`, `configFileFor`), `src/config/presets.ts`
  (`discoverPresets`, `presetDirectories`, `loadPreset`), `src/config/write-config.ts`
  (`updateConfigFile`) and `src/config/environment.ts` mix schemas and resolution with file reads
  and writes, directory discovery and `process.env`.
- Config keeps the schemas, default values, provider/model policy, preset-name validation,
  precedence and selection. Move file reading and writing, and preset directory discovery, to
  adapters behind narrow capabilities (functions or small port interfaces). Environment capture
  moves to the process edge. Config parses the raw values it is given. Parse each input once, at its
  edge; never copy a schema into a caller.
- `src/domain/settings.ts` exports `MAX_STEP_RETRIES = 2` and `RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5000`, and
  `runSettingsFrom` in `load-config.ts` imports them. Move both to config-owned defaults with the
  same values. Domain keeps `RunSettings` and rules such as comparing review cycles with the
  resolved cap. Do not add operator overrides (separate work), and do not let presets set run settings.
- Do not move other caps just because they are numbers. Genuine safety and stopping rules stay in domain.
- Error classes stay where they are for now; a later issue reassigns them. Keep returning the same
  `ConfigInvalid` values.

## Done when

- [ ] No file under `src/config/` imports `node:fs` or reads `process.env`
      (`grep -rnE "node:fs|process\.env" src/config --include=*.ts | grep -v spec` finds nothing).
- [ ] `src/domain/settings.ts` no longer exports the retry defaults; config supplies 2 and 5000 ms.
- [ ] Existing config, preset and environment behavior tests pass. New tests cover the moved I/O
      through fakes or temporary directories.
- [ ] The verification below passes.

## Verification

From the repository root using the pinned Node version (`volta` in `package.json`):

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
npm run format:check
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

No check may start an agent on the host or publish to GitHub. In the PR, state which owner each
moved concept now belongs to and why.


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/55

context.repoSummary:
Configuration currently mixes Zod policy with synchronous filesystem access in src/config/load-config.ts and presets.ts; write-config.ts merges existing JSON objects and persists them with write-file-atomic. Missing repository config defaults to {}, while an explicitly selected missing file fails. Presets resolve repository > home > XDG > builtin, deduplicate directories, preserve broken higher-precedence winners, and replace whole role configurations without changing run settings. Named loading ignores unrelated malformed presets. environment.ts already accepts raw environment values rather than reading process.env, but calls node:os homedir() for fallback; process capture currently lives in src/cli/with-app.ts. Preserve empty-as-unset behavior, telemetry parsing, and environment-over-saved-credential precedence.

Main integration points are cli/with-app.ts (repository checks, environment/credential/config loading, preset selection, container creation), cli/commands/presets.ts, and app/init-sandbox.ts (config reads and updates). domain/settings.ts exports MAX_STEP_RETRIES=2 and RETRY_DELAY_MS=5000, consumed by config's runSettingsFrom; domain also owns RunSettings and independent stopping caps that must remain there. The application-boundaries spec assigns schemas/defaults/selection to config, filesystem capabilities to adapters, process capture to the external edge, and preparation/lifetime policy to app; this slice does not require the broader composition/container refactor. Keep existing ConfigInvalid classes and messages.

Adjacent Vitest specs cover config defaults/errors, atomic-update behavior, preset precedence and filesystem edge cases, environment parsing, and CLI preparation. Use fakes or temporary directories for extracted I/O and retain schema parsing at its owning edge. Follow .claude/rules, update docs/architecture.html, docs/workflow-ownership.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and affected path references; dependency policy belongs in the existing Dependency Cruiser configuration and scripts/check-dependencies fixtures. Verification uses pinned Node 26.13.0 and the requested dependency lint, lint, typecheck, tests, build, formatting and validate -- --skip test:mutation checks.

plan.summary: Separate configuration policy from filesystem and process access while preserving all observable behavior. Config retains schemas, defaults, provider/model policy, preset validation, precedence and selection; adapters own file access, atomic persistence and directory discovery. Move retry defaults of 2 attempts and 5000 ms from domain to config without introducing operator overrides.
plan.approach: Extract narrow filesystem capabilities and keep configuration parsing and resolution independently testable. Adapters read external data and invoke config-owned parsing once at the input boundary; callers receive typed results without copying schemas. Preserve missing repository configuration defaulting to {}, explicitly selected missing-file failures, existing ConfigInvalid tags and messages, and atomic updates that retain unrelated keys and reject non-object JSON. Separate preset location discovery and filesystem probing from config-owned ordering, deduplication, name validation and winner selection. Preserve repository > home > XDG > builtin precedence, broken higher-precedence winners, named loading that ignores unrelated malformed presets, and whole-role replacement without changing run settings. Capture OS home-directory fallback alongside process inputs and pass it into environment parsing, preserving empty-as-unset handling, telemetry and environment-over-saved-credential precedence. Update existing preparation, preset-listing and init integration points without changing operation ordering, cancellation, credential consent or resource lifetime. Architectural mismatches to resolve during design: environment.ts already avoids process.env but still calls homedir(); configFileFor is pure path selection rather than filesystem I/O, so it need not move wholesale; presetDirectories combines location mechanics with precedence policy and must be split rather than relocated unchanged. Current preparation remains in cli/with-app.ts and composition in app/container.ts, whereas the full spec assigns preparation policy to app and wiring to composition; this slice should supply the new capabilities through existing wiring without undertaking the deferred container refactor. Capability placement must also respect the current ports-only-depend-on-domain rule and avoid a config-to-adapter cycle: use narrow function contracts or portable port types, not ports importing JigConfig or Preset from config. Keep error classes in their current locations and domain safety caps unchanged. Retain behavior coverage, move filesystem cases to adapter specs using temporary directories or fakes, and add disk-free policy tests where needed. Update ownership documentation and affected path references; express any dependency restrictions in the existing Dependency Cruiser configuration and fixtures. Verify using pinned Node 26.13.0 with lint:dependencies, lint, typecheck, test, build, format:check and validate -- --skip test:mutation, plus the requested config I/O absence check. Verification must neither launch host agents nor publish to GitHub. The implementation PR should explain each moved concept's owner and any deliberate interim boundary.
affectedAreas: src/config/load-config.ts: separate loading mechanics from schemas, file-selection policy and resolved settings; supply config-owned retry defaults.
src/config/presets.ts: separate directory and file access from preset validation, precedence, selection and role replacement.
src/config/write-config.ts: retain update parsing and merge policy while moving filesystem operations and write-file-atomic persistence to adapters.
src/config/environment.ts: accept externally captured home-directory fallback and retain environment parsing and credential precedence.
src/domain/settings.ts: remove retry-default exports while retaining RunSettings and independent stopping rules.
src/adapters/: add focused configuration-file and preset filesystem implementations, including packaged preset location resolution.
src/ports/ or narrow capability contracts: define only the external operations required, without outward type dependencies.
src/cli/with-app.ts, src/cli/commands/presets.ts, src/app/init-sandbox.ts and relevant wiring: consume extracted capabilities while preserving preparation and lifecycle behavior.
Adjacent config, environment, preset, CLI and init specs; new adapter specs covering missing files, filesystem failures, precedence edge cases and atomic updates.
.dependency-cruiser.mjs, scripts/check-dependencies.mjs and scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts: enforce any newly established dependency boundaries through the existing pipeline.
docs/architecture.html, docs/workflow-ownership.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and existing guides referencing moved paths: document current ownership and locations.
